description.para: Users can define their own; these are common examples.

detaileddescription.para: Stop mode — slower wakeup, lower power

briefdescription.para: Enter low-power mode. Implement for your platform.

detaileddescription.para: For Cortex-M: SYN_SLEEP_LIGHT → WFI, SYN_SLEEP_DEEP → STOP mode. Must return when an interrupt wakes the MCU.

simplesect.para: The tickless scheduler calls this inside a critical section (interrupts masked). The implementation must use a sleep instruction that wakes on pending-but-masked interrupts (WFI on Cortex-M) and must NOT re-enable interrupts itself.

detaileddescription.para: Safe to call from ISR context. The |= on the volatile mask is a load-modify-store, so without a critical section a preempting ISR's lock update would be overwritten by the stale store (lost lock — the CPU could then sleep through an active transfer).
Safe to call from ISR context — see syn_sleep_lock().

briefdescription.para: Check if a specific lock is held.

simplesect.para: true if the lock is active.

briefdescription.para: Check if any lock is held.

simplesect.para: true if any lock is active.

detaileddescription.para: If no locks are held and sleep is enabled, calls syn_port_sleep().

simplesect.para: true if we actually slept, false if vetoed.

parameterdescription.para: true to enable, false to disable.

detaileddescription.para: Coordinates sleep entry with the scheduler. When all tasks are idle (or only timer-blocked), the system can enter a low-power mode. Clients can veto sleep by holding a "stay awake" lock.

listitem.para: Each subsystem that needs the CPU awake holds a lock.
When all locks are released, the scheduler calls syn_sleep_enter() which invokes the port sleep function.
Interrupts wake the MCU, and the scheduler resumes.
